Traditional Dried Pea Soup

Served at: Feast of the Ass

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 1 hour 30 min

Dried Pea Soup is a hearty, comforting dish traditionally served during the Feast of the Ass, a medieval festival celebrating the humble donkey and its role in biblical stories. This soup reflects the humble origins of the festival and is enjoyed as a warming meal during the colder season when the feast is observed.

Ingredients

  • 1 lb (450 g) dried split peas, rinsed
  • 8 cups (1.9 L) water or vegetable broth
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 2 carrots, diced
  • 2 celery stalks, diced
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1 tsp dried thyme
  • Salt and black pepper to taste
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • Optional: 4 oz (115 g) diced ham or smoked sausage

Method

  1. In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat.
  2. Add chopped onion, carrots, and celery; sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
  3. Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
  4. Stir in the rinsed dried peas, bay leaf, and thyme.
  5. Pour in the water or vegetable broth and bring to a boil.
  6. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
  7. If using, add diced ham or smoked sausage halfway through cooking.
  8. Once peas are tender and soup has thickened, remove bay leaf.
  9. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
  10. Use an immersion blender to puree part of the soup for a creamier texture, if desired.
  11. Serve hot with crusty bread.

Tips

  • For a vegetarian version, omit the ham or sausage and use vegetable broth.
  • Soak peas overnight to reduce cooking time.
  • Add a splash of vinegar or lemon juice at the end to brighten flavors.
